$comment: ADJUDICATION OF THE SEMANTIC CANDIDATE SWEEP.
D4.20 falsified the pronoun scan. D4.21 replaced it with mechanism detectors and immediately
reproduced the same disease one level up: the first run flagged 59 new candidates, of which 34
were artefacts of four detector defects — `majority` matching 'the age of majority', `Recipient`
matching 'recipient GSTIN', `assign\w*` matching every copyright assignment in the corpus, and
`proportion` matching vesting over TIME rather than division among PEOPLE.
A detector that cannot be wrong has not been tested, so every surviving candidate is adjudicated
here with a verdict and a reason. The verdicts are mine, read off the shipped clause text; they
are a reading and need an advocate, exactly like the shape assignments in nparty-shapes.json.
TRUE_CANDIDATE      a question genuinely arises above two parties. Becomes work.
ALREADY_CLASSIFIED  found correctly and already carries a shape. Evidence the detector works.
FALSE_POSITIVE      the marker fired and no cardinality question exists. Reason recorded.
THE SYSTEMATIC FALSE POSITIVE WORTH NAMING. `expiry or termination of this Agreement` is a
TEMPORAL TRIGGER — it says WHEN an obligation bites, not WHO it binds — and it appears in a dozen
clauses that have no cardinality question at all. It is the single largest source of noise in the
INSTRUMENT_CONTINUATION mechanism, and it is the direct analogue of 'between the Parties' in the
old scan: a phrase that looks structural and is merely idiomatic.

adjudications.reason: Assembled from the roster and proved at two, three and four principals. Its appearance here is the detector agreeing with a result established independently.
Same. Both were invisible to the pronoun scan and both are genuinely cardinality-sensitive, which is the clearest evidence the old method under-sampled.
Settled on cardinality, open on allocation — governed by allocation-semantics.json. The detector firing on DIVIDED_QUANTITY is correct and points at the axis that is still open.

adjudications.question: Where the instrument ends as to one party but continues between the others, which obligations survive, and between whom?
adjudications.reason: This is DOWNSTREAM OF AN ALREADY-OPEN DECISION. TERMINATION_FOR_DEFAULT_SCOPE asks whether a default ends the instrument or only one relationship; survival then asks what is left standing afterwards, and the answer differs under every candidate treatment. 24 families — the highest-exposure unclassified clause in the portfolio once identity and signature are removed.
adjudications.candidate_shape: PAIRWISE_RIGHT, pending confirmation that it is not an independent question

adjudications.question: Reserved matters require 'the unanimous agreement of the Founders' and everything else a majority. With two founders unanimity and majority are the same thing; with three they are not, and a two-founder deadlock has no majority at all.
adjudications.reason: The clause already speaks in N-party vocabulary, which is why it needs classifying rather than rewriting. Note the converse defect: at two founders 'majority' is unreachable.

adjudications.question: Board seats and voting rights allocated among N shareholders rather than two.
adjudications.reason: Board composition is an allocation of control. Companies Act, 2013 s.149 and s.152 govern appointment; who nominates which director is exactly the kind of question that has one answer at two shareholders and several at three.

adjudications.question: Same mechanism as board composition, for investor-appointed seats.
adjudications.reason: Likely resolves with CORP_BOARD_COMPOSITION_001 as one decision rather than two.

adjudications.question: Drag-along is definitionally an N-party mechanism: a majority compels a minority to sell. At two shareholders there is no minority to drag that is not simply the other party.
adjudications.reason: A clause whose entire purpose presupposes more than two holders, sitting in a corpus that assumes two.
adjudications.incidental_defect: The shipped text reads 'the Majority Shareholders, holding more than 100% of the issued and paid-up share capital' — a rendering defect in the drag threshold, independent of cardinality and worth fixing on its own.

adjudications.question: A liquidation waterfall distributes a finite pool. With more than two holders the order and the pro rata share both become live.
adjudications.reason: Same family of question as LIABILITY_CAP_APPORTIONMENT and differs in money at three.

adjudications.question: 'The aggregate liability of the Guarantor' — with co-guarantors, is the cap each, shared, or joint and several?
adjudications.reason: Directly governed: Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.146 makes co-sureties liable to contribute equally in the absence of contract, and s.147 addresses unequal sums. So unlike the liability cap, this one has a statutory default the instrument may be displacing without saying so.

adjudications.question: 'Entitle the Landlord to terminate this Agreement forthwith' — with co-tenants, does one tenant's unauthorised assignment end the tenancy for all of them?
adjudications.reason: The PAIRWISE_RIGHT question in a different family. Also the only clause in the corpus where 'assign this Agreement' survives the narrowed succession test, which is the mechanism working as intended.

adjudications.question: Stamp duty and registration charges 'borne in the manner agreed by the Parties' — among three, in what shares?
adjudications.reason: An unattributed division of a real cost, which is the economic-allocation problem of invariant 63 appearing in a second place.

adjudications.question: Assignor indemnifies Assignee — with co-assignors, severally or jointly?
adjudications.reason: Same shape as INDEMNITY_APPORTIONMENT; probably resolves with it rather than separately.

adjudications.question: Guarantor indemnifies Creditor — with co-guarantors, how apportioned?
adjudications.reason: Folds into GUARANTEE_OBLIGATION_001 and Contract Act s.146.

adjudications.question: In a multi-party NDA, is each party both Discloser and Recipient as to every other, pairwise?
adjudications.reason: Seven NDA clauses share this one question and should be ONE decision, not seven. Likely RECIPROCAL_SEVERAL and therefore determined — but 'likely' is not a classification, and the NDA family admits a third principal today.

adjudications.question: 'A mutually agreed escrow agent' — agreed by all parties or by the two principals?
adjudications.reason: Almost certainly CONSENT_OR_NOTICE_TO_OTHERS and determined. Recorded so the cheap ones are visibly cheap.

adjudications.question: One co-licensee's breach of permitted use entitling termination against all.
adjudications.reason: Same question as RENT_SUBLEASE_001; folds into it.

Matched 'on the expiry or termination of this Agreement, the Processor shall...'. That is a TEMPORAL TRIGGER — it fixes when erasure is due, not who is bound. The obligation is already distributive across any number of processors. No cardinality question.
Same temporal trigger: 'Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement, the Tenant shall deliver up possession.' Handing back the premises does not change with the number of tenants.

Matched 'expressly agreed by the Parties to include the following excluded categories'. The parties agreeing a DEFINITION is not a decision that party count affects — the same categories are excluded however many of them there are.

adjudications.question: A waiver is effective only if 'signed by or on behalf of' the party granting it. Where there are more than two parties, does one party's waiver of a right extinguish that right for the others, or only as between the waiving party and the one it indulged?
adjudications.reason: Found by SAMPLING THE CLAUSES THIS PROBE HAD CLEARED, not by the probe itself — which is why the mechanism now exists. 25 families, and the two readings are indistinguishable at two parties because there is nobody else whose rights could survive the waiver.

adjudications.question: Stamp duty and registration charges 'shall be borne equally by the Parties'. Equally between two is half each; equally among three is a third each — but the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 s.29 allocates duty by instrument type irrespective of what the parties agree, so the clause may be dividing something it cannot divide.
adjudications.reason: A DEMONSTRATED FALSE NEGATIVE of this probe's first repaired run: the pattern knew 'shared equally' and not 'borne equally', so a divided quantity in 22 documents was reported as carrying no mechanism at all. It is recorded here as a finding about the METHOD as much as about the clause.
adjudications.candidate_shape: Likely determined — 'equally' generalises without a choice — but likely is not a classification.

note: Five NDA clauses are folded into NDA_CONFIDENTIAL_INFORMATION_SCOPE_001 via `resolves_with` rather
than adjudicated separately, because they raise ONE question between them. Counting them
individually would inflate the candidate set with the same finding six times.
PRECISION AND RECALL, BOTH MEASURED RATHER THAN CLAIMED.
Precision: the first run produced 59 candidates, of which 34 were artefacts of four detector
defects. Raw precision about 42 percent; after repair, 3 false positives in 27 — about 89 percent.
Recall: sampling four clauses the repaired probe had CLEARED found two real candidates it had
missed — CORE_STAMP_AND_COSTS_001 (22 families) and CORE_WAIVER_001 (25 families). A 50 percent
hit rate on a sample of four is not a recall estimate, but it is proof that the 108 clauses this
probe flags with nothing are NOT a clean bill of health. Absence of a marker is not absence of a
mechanism — which is exactly what D4.20 established about pronouns, now demonstrated about this
The summary is recomputed from the adjudications by tests/npartyCandidates.test.mjs rather than
maintained by hand, because the first version of this block said 15 true candidates over a list of 14.
